body:
Good morning, Kern County. It's a clear, mild Wednesday — 70 degrees at Meadows Field right now, headed for a high near 89 with clean air and no alerts on the board. The story of the day is the Supreme Court's decision to block new Postal Service ballot-handling rules before the 2026 election season, a ruling that matters deeply in a county where nine of every ten votes are cast by mail. Settle in with your coffee — there's a lot to cover, from an overnight garage fire to a full week of meetings and music downtown.

## The Kern Overnight

Overnight crews in Bakersfield had a full plate, and the biggest call came just after midnight. Multiple callers reported a garage fire on the Planz Road block, attached to a house and already burning into the home. The full response rolled in — two trucks, an engine and two battalion chiefs — and crews got the flames out, but the address wasn't done yet: a vehicle was reported on fire there about 40 minutes later, and fire debris was cleared from the area before dawn.

Around 1 a.m., officers headed south of the city near the river on reports of shots fired. A second caller said the situation was still active and that someone outside was carrying a firearm. One person was wounded in the leg, and a tourniquet was applied at 1:04 a.m.

Earlier in the evening, deputies and search-and-rescue units were sent to Westdale Park around 10 p.m. after a caller reported a woman in the water near the California Aqueduct; crews made a long approach on foot across the park toward the water. Minutes later, fire crews responded to a home on the Meacham Road block where residents reported a major gas leak inside the house. And late in the night, officers searching east Bakersfield railroad tracks for a missing person at risk closed in on foot, asking whether train traffic needed to be stopped; the tracks were placed under manual control while they worked the area.

The rest of the log had its quieter moments: a small fire behind a Kern County ranch property around 9 p.m. that crews found dying down and cleared with nothing more; a weapons call behind a convenience store on the South Union Avenue block at 11:06 p.m.; a 12:45 a.m. standoff near Center and Prospect Streets, where a teenager barricaded himself in a bedroom after assaulting his parents and the call came in from a group home line; a Boron 911 hang-up around midnight in which the caller rambled about a man trying to open a door and nobody answered the callback; a disturbance on the Stockdale Highway block at 1:13 a.m. involving a woman heard yelling in a bank parking lot; and a robbery report on the Pacific Street block at 1:38 a.m.

## Today's weather

It's 70 degrees at Meadows Field this morning, with today's high expected near 89 and an overnight low around 62. There are no active weather alerts for Kern County, and the air quality reading sits at 47 — squarely in the "good" range and a welcome change from hazy summer days. No active fires are listed in this morning's conditions report, so expect a textbook September valley day: sunny and warm through the afternoon, cooling off comfortably after sundown. It's a good day to get outside.

## Top stories

**In a report from 23ABC, the U.S. Supreme Court has blocked new Postal Service ballot-handling rules from taking effect before the 2026 elections — a ruling with outsized stakes in Kern County, where nine of every ten voters who cast a June primary ballot did so by mail, even as turnout reached only about 32 percent of registered voters.** The proposed rules would have required election offices to use scannable envelopes, assign a unique barcode to every voter, and feed basic voter information through a USPS portal, with noncompliant mailings at risk of being returned before they ever reached a mailbox; Justice Brett Kavanaugh wrote that the Postal Service may have the authority to impose such requirements, but that local election officials simply did not have enough time to implement them before the fall. Ian Anderson, a political science professor at Taft and Bakersfield College, told 23ABC the decision came down to feasibility, not legality — and that the deeper concern is how few people participate at all; the station's report also checked in with Bakersfield residents Spencer McNabb and her father Josh, who vote by mail.

**According to KGET 17, Golden West Casino has put a construction project north of Bakersfield on hold.** The pause stops the planned work for now, and the station's report offered no details on what prompted the decision or when the project might resume.

**23ABC reports that Bakersfield College kicked off Hispanic Heritage Month with a campuswide celebration full of color, music and community.** Arvin Mayor Olivia Calderon delivered the keynote, Bakersfield-based bilingual band Velorio performed live, and the campus served up free food from chips and salsa and aguas frescas to a casserole dish, all under this year's theme, "unidos, somos mas" — "together, we are more." The observance carries special weight in Kern County, where more than 58 percent of residents are Hispanic or Latino; Iran Giles, an AB540 worker at the college, told the station her parents left Mexico to give her a better life and the event strengthened her resolve to build a career in human services, while program manager Isabel Castañeda described the celebration as a vivid expression of the community's story and culture.

**KGET 17 reports that diesel prices have climbed to new highs across Kern County, with the warning that drivers should brace for more pain at the pump.** The increase is the latest squeeze on a region where freight, farm work and commuting all run on diesel.

**Bakersfield Now reports that a woman was killed in a solo-vehicle rollover crash on southbound I-5 near Castaic.** The crash happened along the corridor many Kern County residents travel when heading to Los Angeles County, though the station's brief report released no further details.

**Downtown Bakersfield business owners are weighing their next investments after the closure of longtime staple Uricchio's, 23ABC reports.** Tami Slawson of Too Fat Sandwiches told the station the math of staying open gets harder every month — electricity costs have climbed steeply, and she refuses to sacrifice quality by switching to cheaper ingredients. Gabe Uolla, chair of the Downtown Business Association and owner of In Your Wildest Dreams, pointed to the organization's workshops at the Bell Tower covering everything from HR and marketing to insurance and operations, and said grants from the state and county can help businesses on the edge of closing; one closure, he noted, can also clear the way for a new shop to take root downtown.

**KGET 17 reports the Kern County Sheriff's Office has released its August crime statistics, with zero homicide calls logged for the month.** The department's monthly posting showed no homicides reported during August, a notable entry in its continuing tally of countywide calls.

## Something good

There's a new Goodwill in the northwest, and the community turned out for it. The Bakersfield Chamber of Commerce joined Goodwill to cut the ribbon on the new Rosedale store — a grand opening that gives the neighborhood a welcome new retail destination and a bright spot on the local retail landscape. It's a small thing, but a new storefront opening its doors is always a good sign in this valley.

## Coming up this week

It's a busy public-meeting week, starting with a doubleheader today at City Hall: the Bakersfield City Council meets at 3:30 p.m. and again at 5:15 p.m. Thursday brings the Planning Commission at 5:30 p.m., and the committee calendar picks up again Monday at noon with the Finance, Economic Development and Jobs Committee. Tuesday at noon, a meeting dedicated to homelessness is on the schedule, keeping a conversation at the center of local policy in front of the public.

On the entertainment side, the Fox Theater has a full slate. The "It's A 2000s Party" takes the stage Friday night, and the Cults & Classics series returns Monday, September 21, with "What Ever Happened to Baby Jane?" The theater keeps the momentum going into the following week with Montreal indie act Men I Trust and special guest Evan Wright on Wednesday, September 23, comedian Mike Sherm on Saturday, September 26, and the cult favorite "Young Frankenstein" in the Cults & Classics series on October 5.
